 SELECT DISTINCT ON (snapshot->>'workspace_id',snapshot->>'kind',snapshot->>'id') snapshot,id,baseline
 FROM jsonb_to_recordset($1::jsonb) AS b(id bigint,snapshot jsonb,baseline boolean)
 WHERE snapshot IS NOT NULL ORDER BY snapshot->>$2,snapshot->>$3,snapshot->>$4,baseline,id DESC
), eligible AS MATERIALIZED (
 SELECT c.*,f.snapshot AS previous FROM candidates c LEFT JOIN metric_snapshot_facts f
 ON f.workspace_id=(c.snapshot->>$5)::uuid AND f.source_kind=c.snapshot->>$6 AND f.source_id=(c.snapshot->>$7)::uuid
 WHERE f.source_id IS NULL OR (NOT c.baseline AND (f.baseline OR c.id>f.sequence))
), changes AS (
 SELECT snapshot,$8 AS sign FROM eligible UNION ALL SELECT previous,$9 FROM eligible WHERE previous IS NOT NULL
), expanded AS (
 SELECT (snapshot->>$10)::uuid AS workspace_id,(snapshot->>$11)::uuid AS journey_id,(snapshot->>$12)::date AS cohort_day,(snapshot->>$13)::uuid AS version_id,v->>$14 AS dimension,v->>$15 AS dimension_key,v->>$16 AS metric,(v->>$17)::double precision*sign AS value
 FROM changes CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(snapshot->$18) v

 INSERT INTO journey_cohort_metrics SELECT workspace_id,journey_id,cohort_day,version_id,dimension,dimension_key,metric,sum(value) FROM expanded GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6,7 HAVING sum(value)<>$19

database_wait_sampling.meaning: Sampled active-backend occupancy, not exact wait duration. CPU_or_not_waiting does not establish CPU saturation. Query IDs correlate with statement statistics; inactive transactions and diagnostic connection are excluded.

environment.postgres: PostgreSQL 17.11 on aarch64-unknown-linux-musl, compiled by gcc (Alpine 15.2.0) 15.2.0, 64-bit

method: Real loopback HTTP ingestion and actual PostgreSQL runtime/delivery/projector, warm local Docker database. Fixture creates 1,000 inactive draft journeys and synthetic customers. Stage A reaches the requested number of simultaneously WAITING durable executions (MVP threshold: 10,000). Stage B moves only isolated fixture timer deadlines to a declared burst or spread beginning five seconds ahead, then lets real workers process. No frozen clock, SMTP or LLM requests. Completion polling interval is 1s; Go memory includes benchmark client+API+worker in one process. Two transient mock provider outcomes (429/500) are injected. Up to five serial authenticated UI reads/sec rotate across nine routes, including journey insights and drilldowns, throughout loaded phases; requests are not an open-loop saturation test. pg_stat_statements records top-level statement execution (including trigger cost); client network/round-trip time is not included. Timer lateness measures step completion after due_at, not claim time. EXPLAIN probes do not modify job state. Metrics/SQL timing and bounded queue sampling are enabled; no trace exporter is started. Optional pacing and provider delay are declared in the report. Successful-attempt latency excludes earlier 429 waits; logical latency includes them.

Plans.Filter: ((due_at <= '2026-11-19 20:13:41.470088+00'::timestamp with time zone) AND (status = 'SCHEDULED'::text) AND (mode = 'LIVE'::text) AND ((((workspace_id)::text || '/'::text) || provider) <> ALL ('{}'::text[])) AND (SubPlan 1))

work_cost.meaning: PostgreSQL work per 1,000 executions that finished the stage (stage A: reached the durable wait; stage B: completed with the message accepted and projections caught up). CPU is the database container's cgroup usage, so it holds regardless of what else runs on the host. SQL figures cover top-level statements, including the benchmark's own reads, polling and EXPLAIN probes.
